headline: 579 tourists missing after deadly floods and mudslides in Nepal
summary: Foreign nationals from 28 countries are among the missing as Bangladesh offers assistance to the disaster-stricken nation.
details: A devastating series of flash floods and mudslides in Nepal has left 579 tourists missing, according to the latest data from Nepal Police reported by BBC Nepali.
Of those missing, 466 are foreign nationals from 28 different countries, while 113 are Nepali citizens.
The missing foreigners include 54 citizens from the United States and 33 from the United Kingdom.
Search and rescue operations are ongoing in the flood-affected border areas, though efforts are hampered by rugged terrain and severed communication lines.
Adverse weather conditions have further complicated the rescue missions as teams struggle to reach isolated settlements.
Bangladesh has expressed its grief and solidarity with Nepal, offering assistance to help the country manage the aftermath of the disaster.
caption:
579 tourists are missing after catastrophic floods and mudslides hit Nepal, including hundreds of foreign nationals from 28 countries.

A devastating series of flash floods and mudslides in Nepal has left 579 tourists missing, according to the latest data from Nepal Police reported by BBC Nepali.

Of those missing, 466 are foreign nationals from 28 different countries, while 113 are Nepali citizens.

The missing foreigners include 54 citizens from the United States and 33 from the United Kingdom.

Search and rescue operations are ongoing in the flood-affected border areas, though efforts are hampered by rugged terrain and severed communication lines.

Adverse weather conditions have further complicated the rescue missions as teams struggle to reach isolated settlements.

Bangladesh has expressed its grief and solidarity with Nepal, offering assistance to help the country manage the aftermath of the disaster.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Jamuna TV, Prothom Alo, The Daily Star

headline_marked: Police recover gold earring after [[snatcher swallows jewelry]] in Dhaka
headline: Police recover gold earring after snatcher swallows jewelry in Dhaka
summary: A traffic police sergeant caught a thief who had swallowed a stolen gold earring to hide the evidence before being apprehended.
details: A gold earring was snatched from Nipa Akter as she was traveling by rickshaw to see a doctor in Dhaka's Jatrabari area on Wednesday evening.
Hearing the victim's screams, Traffic Police Sergeant Imran Mridha chased and apprehended the suspect, identified as 28-year-old Md. Selim, a resident of Rayerbag.
When police searched the suspect, the stolen earring was not found. During questioning, Selim admitted that he had swallowed the jewelry before being caught.
Police then induced the suspect to vomit, which successfully recovered the gold earring from his stomach.
Both the suspect and the victim have been sent to Jatrabari Police Station for further legal action.
caption:
He swallowed the gold earring to hide the evidence, but police didn't let it get away.

A gold earring was snatched from Nipa Akter as she was traveling by rickshaw to see a doctor in Dhaka's Jatrabari area on Wednesday evening.

Hearing the victim's screams, Traffic Police Sergeant Imran Mridha chased and apprehended the suspect, identified as 28-year-old Md. Selim, a resident of Rayerbag.

When police searched the suspect, the stolen earring was not found. During questioning, Selim admitted that he had swallowed the jewelry before being caught.

Police then induced the suspect to vomit, which successfully recovered the gold earring from his stomach.

Both the suspect and the victim have been sent to Jatrabari Police Station for further legal action.
